LESSON: STATISTICAL METHODS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Practical Geography
Topic 1.3: Statistical Methods
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Statistical Methods, part of Practical Geography in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How do we use statistics in day-to- day life? 2. Why are statistical methods important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Statistical Methods together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The skill of research is enhanced as the learner conducts library research on the

limitations of statistics in explaining geographical facts and writes notes.

● Creativity and Imagination: The skill of asking questions is exhibited as the learner role plays the methods of data

collection.

● Learning to Learn: The skill of investigation is developed as the learner carries out research within the school on a selected

geographical topic.

Values:
● Integrity: Learner exhibits honesty as they carry out research within the school on a selected geographical topic.

● Respect: Learner expresses patience as they brainstorm on the importance of statistics in Geography and makes

presentation in class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Critical Thinking: Learner discusses the methods of data analysis and interpretation and makes presentation in class.

● Social Cohesion: Learner works with others as they brainstorm on the importance of statistics in Geography.

9

● Road Safety: Learner Uses methods of data analysis and data from roads and compute road injuries in Kenyan roads and

present in class.

Suggested Learning Resources

Local and extended environment, digital devices with assistive technology, Approved textbooks, Printed and braile resources,

charts, tactile charts and diagrams, Flipcharts, Display boards, Whiteboards and marker pens, Smart boards, tactile models of

different methods of data presentations(Combined bar and line graphs, Comparative/group /multiple bar graphs).
